name: The United Kingdom
intro: The four nations of the UK, the difference between Great Britain and the UK, how the country is governed, and life and diversity in British society.
sammendrag:
## Four nations, one kingdom

The **United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland** – the **UK** for short – consists of four nations: **England**, **Scotland**, **Wales** and **Northern Ireland**. Their capitals are **London**, **Edinburgh**, **Cardiff** and **Belfast**. London is also the capital of the whole UK.

People often mix up the names. **Great Britain** is the largest island and includes England, Scotland and Wales. The **UK** also includes Northern Ireland. The **British Isles** is a geographical name for Great Britain, Ireland and many smaller islands. The **Republic of Ireland** is an independent country and not part of the UK.

## Government

The UK is a **constitutional monarchy**. The **King** is head of state, but he has little real political power. The country is governed by **Parliament** in London, which has two chambers: the elected **House of Commons** and the **House of Lords**. The leader of the largest party in the House of Commons usually becomes **Prime Minister**. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland also have their own parliaments or assemblies that decide on matters like education and health.

## The UK and Europe

The UK was a member of the **European Union** from 1973. In a **referendum** in 2016, a small majority voted to leave, and the UK left the EU in 2020. This process is known as **Brexit**. It was, and still is, a much debated topic in British politics.

## Languages and identity

English is the main language, but **Welsh** is spoken by many people in Wales, and **Scottish Gaelic** and **Irish** are also used. Many people feel strongly connected to their own nation and call themselves Scottish, Welsh or English as well as British. The flag, the **Union Jack**, combines the crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland.

## A diverse society

The UK is a **multicultural** society. Many people have roots in former colonies in the Caribbean, Africa and South Asia, and more recently in other European countries. Big cities like London, Birmingham and Manchester are home to people from all over the world, which is reflected in food, music, religion and language.

## Culture

Britain has given the world famous writers like **William Shakespeare** and **J.K. Rowling**, bands like **The Beatles**, and sports like **football**, **rugby** and **cricket**. The **BBC** is a well-known public broadcaster. Traditions like afternoon tea, fish and chips and the Premier League are part of the image many people have of Britain, but everyday life is as varied as in any modern country.

quiz.text: Which four nations make up the UK?
options: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
quiz.explain: The UK consists of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. The Republic of Ireland is a separate country.

quiz.text: What is the capital of Scotland?
quiz.explain: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland. Glasgow is the largest city.

quiz.text: What is the difference between Great Britain and the UK?
options: Great Britain is bigger than the UK
The UK also includes Northern Ireland
quiz.explain: Great Britain is the island with England, Scotland and Wales. The UK adds Northern Ireland.

quiz.text: What is the elected chamber of the British Parliament called?
quiz.explain: Members of the House of Commons are elected by the people.

options: The UK leaving the European Union
quiz.explain: Brexit is short for “Britain exit”, the UK leaving the EU after the 2016 referendum.

quiz.text: Which language is spoken by many people in Wales?
quiz.explain: Welsh is a Celtic language with official status in Wales.

quiz.text: What type of government does the UK have?
quiz.explain: The King is head of state, but Parliament and the government hold the political power.

quiz.text: Who becomes Prime Minister in the UK?
options: Usually the leader of the largest party in the House of Commons
quiz.explain: The Prime Minister is usually the leader of the party that can command a majority in the House of Commons.
William Shakespeare is one of the most famous writers in the English language.

quiz.text: Why is the UK a multicultural society?
options: Because everyone has the same background
Because people with roots in many countries live there
quiz.explain: Immigration from former colonies and other countries has made the UK very diverse.

ekstra.text: The Republic of Ireland is part of the UK.
ekstra.explain: The Republic of Ireland is an independent country. Only Northern Ireland is part of the UK.

ekstra.text: The King of the UK has little real political power.
ekstra.explain: In a constitutional monarchy, elected politicians govern.

ekstra.text: Cardiff is the capital of Wales.
ekstra.explain: Cardiff is the capital and largest city of Wales.

ekstra.text: Scotland has its own parliament that decides on some matters.
ekstra.explain: The Scottish Parliament decides on issues like education and health.

ekstra.text: When did the UK leave the EU?
ekstra.explain: The referendum was in 2016, but the UK formally left the EU in 2020.

ekstra.text: What does the Union Jack combine?
options: The crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland
The flags of all Commonwealth countries
ekstra.explain: The flag combines the crosses of St George, St Andrew and St Patrick.
The British Broadcasting Corporation is a well-known public broadcaster.
